concept.name: Explicit transaction cost
concept.definition: The directly invoiced, observable costs of trading: commissions, exchange and clearing fees, and taxes or duties. They are known (or contractually set) before the trade and appear as line items rather than being inferred from prices.
concept.intuition: Explicit costs are the receipt you can read: commission per share, exchange fee, clearing fee, stamp tax - no estimation required.
concept.mechanics: Brokers charge commissions per share/contract or per notional; exchanges charge per-share execution fees (or pay rebates) per their public fee schedules; clearing agencies charge per-contract clearing fees. Rule 10b-10 confirmations must disclose the remuneration the broker received, making these costs visible to the customer.
concept.formula: Explicit cost = commission + exchange/venue fees + clearing fees + regulatory fees and taxes, summed over the trade.
concept.failure_modes: Explicit costs are small per trade but compound brutally with turnover, silently consuming strategy edge in high-frequency or high-turnover approaches. Fee schedules with tiers and caps also make the marginal cost volume-dependent and easy to mis-estimate.
concept.misconceptions: Zero-commission does not mean zero explicit cost - exchange, clearing, and regulatory fees still apply, and remuneration can be embedded elsewhere (payment for order flow). Explicit costs are also the smaller half of trading cost for large orders; implicit costs usually dominate.
concept.example: Buying 1,000 shares: $1.00 commission + $0.30 exchange/regulatory fees + clearing charges - all printed on the confirm, before any slippage is counted.
